info.title: Bank Orchestrator
info.description:
**Service map** (all mounted under one process, one shared KvStore):

| Prefix | Service | What it owns |
|---|---|---|
| `/governance` | Orchestrator governance | Canon versions, lexicon, tier table, interface rules, CASS stub (CIS-1), SI-1 staging, amendments, veto log, PENDING register |
| `/p1` | Pillar 1 — intake + demo flow | Candidates, scoring/approval/disbursement demo loop, board state, simulation tick |
| `/p2` | Pillar 2 — credit scoring | BRR/PD/LGD/EAD/EL, the versioned BRR→PD grid, early-warning signals, CASS feed contract |
| `/p3` | Pillar 3 — loan execution | Facilities, P2 packets, audit trail, postings, core-banking ledger, reconciliation, lifecycle actions |
| `/p4` | Pillar 4 — prudential layer | Buffer sub-accounts, guarantee-pool adequacy, capital snapshot, IFRS 9 staging, two-track veto, mode gate, pledge intake/release |
| `/bilan` | French-PCG balance sheet | Live Actif/Passif from the shared store, invariant checks, memo items |

**Read the API top-down:** create a candidate in **Pillar 1**, submit → score →
approve → disburse through the demo loop, then watch **Pillar 3** facilities/postings
and **Pillar 4** buffer/capital/veto update. `GET /p4/veto/consult` is the state
**Pillar 2** must consult before confirming a packet — Pillar 3 never sees a veto.

get.description: Compute the balance sheet live from the shared KvStore.

put.description:
Merge a partial update into ``bilan_config_v1`` and return the result.

This is the only bilan path that writes — to a brand-new KV key, leaving
``p3_state_v1``/``p4_state_v1`` (and therefore ``/ready``) untouched.
Requires ``X-Admin-Token`` and leaves an append-only audit row behind.

The config write and the audit append are two separate KV writes and are
**not atomic**: the config is committed first, then the audit row. If the
audit append fails the error is logged and the response is still 200,
because the caller's change *did* take effect — reporting failure would
invite a retry that then records a spurious second change. A failure of
the config write itself still propagates (no transaction layer is built
here; see ``bug_bilan_fix_round_2.md``, R4).

get.description:
Restart-ok probe — mirrors rt3/rt4: open a fresh Pillar 3 and Pillar 4
runtime over the same KvStore file and assert the rehydrated snapshot is
byte-identical to the persisted blob. 503 when any assertion fails.

get.description: Every posting event P3 captured (disbursements, repayments, fees, losses, recoveries). P3 computes no allocation — events flagged ``routes_allocation_question_to_p4`` carry the allocation question to Pillar 4, which owns all burden-sharing.
Core-banking postings — the system of record. Core banking always wins a reconciliation dispute against the P3 event log; P4 governs only the tolerance.
Compare total P3 posting amounts against the core-banking ledger within a tolerance (default 0.0 — exact match). Returns the unmatched P3 event ids when they differ.

post.description: Open a facility from a confirmed Pillar 2 packet. The packet must pass the confirmation gate (Canon §8.1); a frozen Pillar 4 veto resolves at Pillar 2 and surfaces here as a 409 — P3 never sees a veto event, only a confirmed or withheld packet.

get.description: Live balances of the four Part II sub-accounts: EL Pool (IFRS 9 ECL provisions), ULA Buffer (loss capacity beyond Budgeted Loss), LR (funding-side liquidity), and RP Pool (risk-premium income).

Guarantees received vs the Pillar 2 required pooled-guarantee level. A shortfall paces origination; a shortfall coinciding with a ratio breach triggers the Track 1 veto. Pillar 4 never re-sizes the required level.

The three live prudential ratios: Tier D / RWA (floor 12%), portfolio EL vs the Budgeted Loss (2%), and the Guarantees-Granted/Received ratio, plus their raw inputs (RWA by facility, risk weights, guarantee books).

BilanCheck.title: BilanCheck

BilanConfigUpdate.title: BilanConfigUpdate

BilanConfigView.title: BilanConfigView
BilanConfigView.description:
The stored config plus the cash opening it *resolves* to.

Overriding ``tresorerie_ouverture`` here deliberately changes its meaning:
on :class:`BilanConfig` it is the *configured* opening cash (``None`` =
derive it), on this response it is the value the bilan actually used.

The resolved value alone cannot say which of the two it started as, so
``tresorerie_ouverture_configured`` reports the original ``None``-ness —
a client that needs to know "did a human set this?" reads that flag
(``bug_bilan_fix_round_2.md``, R4).

P2OutputPacket.title: P2OutputPacket
P2OutputPacket.description:
An approved/provisional/conditional output packet from Pillar 2.

Attributes mirror exactly what the Canon says P3 records off the
packet: Model Maturity Stage, BRR-PD grid version, collateral track
(Canon §8.1), plus the confirmation/authorisation flags P3 must gate
on before acting (Canon §8.1, §8.6).

CapitalSnapshotOut.title: CapitalSnapshotOut
CapitalSnapshotOut.description:
Tier D / RWA, portfolio EL, and the G/G ratio with their inputs.

Ratio fields are nullable: the engine returns ``None`` where a
denominator is still zero (e.g. no guarantees received yet).

GovernanceRuling.title: GovernanceRuling
GovernanceRuling.description: An explicit, signed record of a governance decision (SI-1 act).

Pillar2RiskPacket.title: Pillar2RiskPacket
Pillar2RiskPacket.description:
BRR/PD/LGD/EAD/EL packet (standard cadence + event-driven).

Bound to Pillar 4's capital/leverage computation (Derivation Register I-a).

Pillar3Event.title: Pillar3Event
Pillar3Event.description: A typed, immutable Pillar 3 per-loan event fed into the event router.

PledgeSubmission.title: PledgeSubmission
PledgeSubmission.description:
A Pillar 5 submission of a pooled Layer (Tier A / Tier B) pledge position.

The eligible_types/haircut/concentration checks are made against Pillar 4's
ADMISSIBILITY POLICY. The pledge carries its tier; only Tier A / Tier B
positions enter the pool (funding-vs-collateral boundary).

PoolAdequacyOut.title: PoolAdequacyOut
PoolAdequacyOut.description: Guarantees received vs the Pillar 2 required level.

RequiredGuaranteeLevel.title: RequiredGuaranteeLevel
RequiredGuaranteeLevel.description:
Pillar 2's required pooled-guarantee level (R_pool) that P4 monitors.

Pillar 4 NEVER re-sizes this; it only compares guarantees RECEIVED against
it (claude.md §5.4/§5.2, §8.12). Units: admitted contingent-cash-equivalent
value, post-haircut (like-for-like with how P4 measures the pool).
The transport/carrier is BLOCKED by PENDING_TWO_GUARANTEE_LAYER_CONTRACT;
this logical field models the value, not the wire.

StagingSignal.title: StagingSignal
StagingSignal.description:
IFRS 9 staging signal (Stage 1/2/3), P2 -> P4 EL Pool DIRECT (bypasses P3).

A staging migration triggers NO Pillar 3 covenant or freeze - it is purely
a Pillar 4 provisioning event (claude.md §4.4). Wire format PENDING.

VetoConsultOut.title: VetoConsultOut
VetoConsultOut.description: The veto state Pillar 2 must consult before confirming any packet.
